items.title: build_kv_chunk_table assumes every layer holds a KV slab, so no hybrid-attention model can be PCC-checked through the runner
items.body:
Found during Kimi-K3 runner bring-up (#53508). Index: #54814.

## What

Publishing the KV chunk table asserts that the cache's batch dimension equals `num_users * num_my_layers`:

```
AssertionError: cache batch dim 6 != num_users(1) * num_my_layers(24)
```

Kimi-K3 is hybrid: only 24 of its 93 layers are full-attention (MLA); the other 69 are KDA and write no KV slab at all. A 24-layer slice therefore holds **6** MLA layers and allocates 6 cache entries, not 24. The assertion rejects the model outright.

`KimiK3Adapter.allocate_kv_cache` already sizes the cache by `schedule.num_mla_layers` rather than `params.num_layers` — correctly. The table builder is the piece that still assumes one slab per layer.

## Why it matters

This is the only path to scoring PCC on what the runner actually produces. `prefill_producer` locates each cache through the published table (`_read_kv_chunk_table` -> `_verify_resident_slots` -> `_read_slot_kv_and_check_pcc_mla`) and reads it back over UMD. No table, no read-back, no PCC.

Combined with `PREFILL_MOCK_MIGRATION` refusing `num_ranks>1` (each rank would publish a table covering only its own slice), **there is currently no configuration in which a hybrid model can be accuracy-checked end to end through the runner** — multi-rank is refused by design, and single-rank fails this assertion.

Consequences for Kimi-K3 today:

- correctness had to be established **in-process** instead (two transformers on one mesh, output piped directly), which verifies the model but not the socket path
- the `PREFILL_USE_TRACE=1` replay cannot be PCC-checked at all, so tracing has no verified-correct measurement despite capturing and replaying cleanly

## Repro

Any hybrid-attention model, single rank:

```
PREFILL_MOCK_MIGRATION=1 ./models/demos/common/prefill/runners/run_pipeline_prefill.sh \
  <a kimi_k3 rank binding> <host>:1 <iface>
```

Fails during table publish, before serving.

## Suggested fix

Size the table from the same source the cache was allocated from — the model's layer schedule (`num_mla_layers` / the per-layer KV-slot map) rather than the rank's layer count. The adapter already exposes it; the assertion just needs to ask for it instead of assuming a dense stack.

items.title: ttnn.tanh_bw: fp32 path uses a BF16-scoped asymptotic tail, dropping the (1+e^-2x)^-2 factor — up to 65,346 fp32 ULP
items.body:
**Component / Area:** kernels (SFPU) / TTNN eltwise unary_backward

**Issue Type:** Bad Outputs

## Observed

`ttnn.tanh_bw` on a **float32** tensor returns `sech²(x)` values up to **65,346 fp32 ULP**
(relative error 4.96e-03) too large for inputs in `|x| >= 3`. The error appears as a **step
discontinuity** at `|x| = 3.0`: the value jumps by 0.445% of the true result across a seam where
`sech²` is smooth.

| \|x\| | kernel | true sech²(x) | fp32 ULP |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.9999 | 9.87287983e-03 | 9.86800081e-03 | 5,239 (poly side) |
| **3.0000** | **9.91495699e-03** | **9.86603717e-03** | **52,527** (tail side) |
| 3.1192 | — | — | **65,346** (worst) |
| 3.5 | 3.64752789e-03 | 3.64088472e-03 | 28,532 |
| 5.0 | 1.81604119e-04 | 1.81583231e-04 | 1,435 |
| 8.0 | 4.50140703e-07 | 4.50140598e-07 | 4 |

The BF16 path is unaffected (max 1 bf16 ULP), which is why exhaustive BF16 validation passes.

## Mechanism

`ckernel_sfpu_tanh_derivative.h` splits at `CORE_REGION_LIMIT = 3.0f`. The tail branch computes

```cpp
v_elseif(a < TAIL_REGION_LIMIT) {
    // Asymptotic formula exact to 1 BF16 ULP for |x| >= CORE_REGION_LIMIT.
    result = inline_exp_sech2_tail(a);   // = 4·exp(-2|x|)
}
```

i.e. it drops the denominator of the identity the file's own API doc advertises:

```
sech²(x) = 4·exp(-2|x|) / (1 + exp(-2|x|))²      <- tanh_derivative.h:30
result   = 4·exp(-2|x|)                          <- what the tail branch returns
```

Dropping `(1 + y)⁻²` with `y = e^{-2|x|}` costs a **relative** error of `≈ 2y = 2e^{-2|x|}`.
At `|x| = 3` that is `4.96e-03`. In BF16 (spacing 2⁻⁸ ≈ 3.9e-03) that rounds to ≤ 1 ULP, so the
approximation is sound at BF16. In FP32 (spacing 2⁻²⁴) the same relative error is ~5·10⁴ ULP.

The justification in the header is explicitly BF16-scoped —

> For `|x| >= 3.0`, the asymptotic approximation `sech²(x) ≈ 4·exp(-2|x|)` is exact to within
> **1 BF16 ULP** (verified exhaustively).

— but the branch is taken regardless of `is_fp32_dest_acc_en`, even though the same function
already takes that flag (it keys the output rounding on it at the end of the loop). This is the
same shape as #54867: a threshold/approximation validated at BF16 applied unconditionally on the
FP32 path.

Reachability: `tanh_bw_program_factory.cpp:92` sets `fp32_dest_acc_en = true` when the destination
format is `Float32`, and `tanh_derivative.h:41` defaults `is_fp32_dest_acc_en = DST_ACCUM_MODE`.

## Reproduction

`repro.py` (attached below) is a source-faithful fp32 model of
`calculate_tanh_derivative_sech2` — coefficients, Cody-Waite constants and the FTZ guard read
verbatim from the header, `PolynomialEvaluator` evaluated in ascending coefficient order per
`ckernel_sfpu_polyval.h`.

**The model reproduces this file's own published validation numbers**, which is the control for
everything above:

| header claim | model |
|---|---|
| core poly "Max ULP = 1, **99.26% exact**" | max 1 bf16 ULP, **99.26%** exact (32,652/32,894) |
| "Max ULP = 1 across all valid BF16 values" | max 1 bf16 ULP over all finite non-denormal results |

## Suggested fix

The tail branch already computes `E = 4·e^{-2a}`, so `y = E/4` is free and **no second exp is
needed**. Restoring the denominator on the FP32 path only:

```cpp
sfpi::vFloat E = inline_exp_sech2_tail(a);
if constexpr (is_fp32_dest_acc_en) {
    sfpi::vFloat y = E * 0.25f;             // e^{-2a}, free
    sfpi::vFloat d = 1.0f + y;  d = d * d;  // (1 + e^{-2a})^2
    result = E * <reciprocal of d>;
} else {
    result = E;                             // BF16 path unchanged
}
```

This file deliberately makes **no external function calls** (its header says so explicitly:
"No external function calls (`_sfpu_exp_f32_accurate_`, `sfpu_reciprocal_iter`)", and it does not
include `ckernel_sfpu_recip.h`). So the reciprocal should be an inline Newton chain in the same
style as `inline_exp_sech2_tail`, not a call into the recip kernel. Measured that way:

| | worst over \|x\| ∈ [3, 10] | seam jump at 3.0 |
|---|---|---|
| today | 65,346 fp32 ULP | 0.445% |
| denominator restored (inline Newton) | **679 fp32 ULP** | 0.051% |

~96x better, and the residual is the inline exp's own error rather than the formula's — restoring
the identity removes essentially all of the formula error, so further gains would have to come
from the exp, not from this branch. Cost is ~5 extra ops on the FP32 tail path only; the BF16
path keeps its current op count.

I would rather you choose the exact reciprocal sequence and iteration count than assert one — the
numbers above are what I can defend, and I have not tuned it.

## Scope / honest limits

- Found with a **source-faithful fp32 model in numpy, not on silicon** — I do not have Wormhole
  hardware. The model is validated against this file's own published BF16 numbers (above), but I
  would welcome correction if the deployed path differs from the source I modelled.
- **Not** an instance of #52178: that class is saturating input clamps returning a silent
  constant outside a fit domain. Here the tail is a genuine asymptotic approximation whose
  *relative* error is below BF16 resolution but far above FP32 resolution.
- Denormal results (`|x|` ∈ [44.5, 46.5], where `TAIL_REGION_LIMIT = 45` truncates values below
  BF16 min normal) are **excluded** — that is the documented DAZ+FTZ model, not a defect.
- The core polynomial region `|x| < 3` shows ~5·10³ fp32 ULP by the same mechanism (a poly whose
  stated validation is "Max ULP = 1" at BF16). I am reporting only the tail here because the
  tail is where the mechanism is unambiguous and the fix is cheap; the core would need a
  refit rather than an identity restoration.

**Disclosure:** I use AI assistance in my work. Every number above was produced by running the
attached reproduction, and the source lines were read in the repository.

items.title: tril / triu build the triangular mask on the host one element at a time, at 277x a clone
items.body:
**Component / Area:** ttnn eltwise unary (composite)

**Issue Type:** Performance

## Observed

Blackhole p150b, bfloat16, TILE, DRAM interleaved, min of 7.

| N | clone | `tril` | vs clone |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 42.7 us | 841.8 us | 19.7x |
| 1024 | 41.0 us | 3001.2 us | 73.2x |
| 2048 | 73.3 us | 20352.2 us | **277.7x** |

`triu` is the same, 20590.0 us at N=2048. The cost grows superlinearly: doubling
N multiplies the time by 3.6x then 6.8x against 4x the data.

The multiply is not the cost. `multiply(a, a)` on the same tensor is 127.0 us,
1.8x clone. Everything above that is mask construction.

`tril` calls `index_tril<::bfloat16>`
(`ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary/device/unary_composite_op.cpp:309`),
which lands in `index_trilu` at
`ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/functions.hpp:57`:

```cpp
auto output_buffer = std::vector<T>(padded_shape.volume());
...
for (uint32_t itr = 0; itr < iterations; itr++) {
    for (int32_t y = 0; y < padded_shape[penultimate]; y++) {
        for (int32_t x = 0; x < padded_shape[ultimate]; x++) {
            int32_t value = (IS_UPPER) ? (x >= (y + diag)) : (y >= (x - diag));
            output_buffer[index + (y * padded_shape[ultimate]) + x] = static_cast<T>(value);
        }
    }
}
```

The whole mask is allocated and written on the host, one scalar per element, then
transferred and multiplied. At N=2048 that is 4,194,304 host writes plus an 8 MiB
transfer, for a value that is a pure function of the element coordinates.

## Expected

Generate the mask on device. `y >= (x - diag)` depends only on the coordinates,
which the reader already computes per page, so no host buffer and no transfer is
needed.

## Related, and distinct

#53971 and #52038 both concern `tril` / `triu` correctness: the mask being built
as bfloat16 whatever the input dtype, and an `inf` in the masked region becoming
NaN on the fp32 path. Both identify the mask-multiply composition. Neither reports
that the mask is built on the host or what it costs, which is what this issue is
about.

I would like to work on this through the bounty program.

items.title: MatmulMultiCoreReuse silently drops output blocks when num_output_blocks > num_cores
items.body:
### Summary

`MatmulMultiCoreReuseProgramConfig` writes exactly one output block per core. When the program config asks for more output blocks than the compute grid has cores, the surplus blocks are never computed and the tail of the output tensor is left at whatever the buffer already held. There is no error and no warning: the op returns a tensor that is partly correct and partly uninitialized.

Block count is `batch * (M_t / per_core_M) * (N_t / per_core_N)`.

### Repro

Blackhole, 8 devices, grid 11x10 = 110 cores. Per chip: batch 32, `[20, 16] x [16, 4]` tiles (this is the MLA `wkv_b2` shape at the 640-token production chunk), bf16 in / bf8 weights, interleaved L1 activation, interleaved DRAM output.

```python
pc = ttnn.MatmulMultiCoreReuseProgramConfig(
    compute_with_storage_grid_size=(11, 10),
    in0_block_w=2, out_subblock_h=1, out_subblock_w=4,
    per_core_M=5, per_core_N=4,
)   # blocks = 32 * (20/5) * (4/4) = 128 > 110
out = ttnn.linear(act, weight, program_config=pc, memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG, dtype=ttnn.bfloat8_b)
```

PCC vs `torch.matmul` is `-0.000009`, reproducible on 3 consecutive runs. Dropping to `per_core_M=10` (64 blocks, under the core count) gives PCC `0.999917` on the same shape, also reproducible.

### Why it is easy to miss

The failure only shows when the destination buffer does not already contain the right answer. Running any other matmul over the same output buffer first leaves the correct values there, so the partial write reads back as a pass. That is what made this look non-deterministic at first: in a sweep, the same over-subscribed config returned PCC ~0 when it ran first and PCC 0.9999 when it ran after a config that had filled the buffer.

### Suggested fix

`validate_matmul_reuse_sharded_output_block_divisibility` in `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/matmul/device/matmul_device_operation.cpp` already computes `num_output_blocks` and compares it against a core count, but it returns early unless one of the inputs is L1-sharded:

```cpp
if (sharded == nullptr) {
    return;
}
```

With interleaved inputs nothing checks the block count at all. The bound should be validated for interleaved inputs too (against `compute_with_storage_grid_size`), or the factory should give a core more than one block instead of dropping the surplus.

### Impact

`MLA_MATMUL_CONFIG` uses this config type for `wkv_b1` / `wkv_b2` at the 640 slot. The shipped entries stay under the bound (Kimi-K2.6 at 64 heads is 80 blocks, K3 at 96 heads is 96 blocks), so production is not currently affected. A model with more resident heads per device, or any retune that lowers `per_core_M`, crosses it silently.

Found while retuning `test_mla_matmuls.py` for #54761.
